discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in `1544b995b`. `suggestion()` in `candidates.ts` now clips `prompt` to `PROMPT_MAX_CHARS` and `why` to `WHY_MAX_CHARS` before it hashes the id, so rule, model and turn rows all stay inside the published bounds. Text within the limits is unchanged, so the `host-rules.json` parity fixtures keep their ids. `contracts.test.ts` builds rows from a long task title, a status headline and a failing check list, and validates the set and push against `NextTurnSet` and `NextTurnTrayPush`.

Fixed in 85ba54c1e8. When a Skip names a row that sits before the cursor (one New set already paged past), the cursor now moves back by one. Only the skipped row leaves the pool, and the rows on screen stay put. A test pins your sequence: New set, then a late Skip for Verify, leaves Review/Wrap up/Next step in view, and Undo skip brings Verify back to the front. I also fuzzed 4,000 random verb sequences offline against "a skip hides only its row, more drops only the last row, Undo skip brings its row into view". The fuzzer finds this bug without the fix and finds nothing with it.

Valid, fixed in e4b6ea149d.

A polling start line is now dropped only when its own successful end follows it. Starts and ends are paired in order, by command, request ID and client ID, because some clients reuse request IDs (for example `hub-client-1`). As a result:

- A poll that never finished keeps its start line, so a hub that stopped answering still shows up in the report.
- A failed poll keeps both its start and its end.

Added a test for a start with no end, and tightened the existing test to check that a failed poll keeps both lines.

Addressed in the follow-up commit: the new `charges a flat ESTIMATED_TOKENS_PER_IMAGE per image` test asserts the delta for one image is `ESTIMATED_TOKENS_PER_IMAGE` plus the JSON overhead and that payload length leaves the estimate unchanged, with the same payload-length check added to the `createTokenEstimator` test. Removing the per-image term now fails the suite.

Valid, and fixed in 1690c40bf. I removed the cap. Each failure record is what stops its run from falling back to an earlier checkpoint, so failures now persist for the life of the session, as checkpoint history does. Covered by `keeps every failure so no failed run falls back to an earlier checkpoint` in `checkpoint-records.test.ts`; it fails if the cap is put back.

Valid, added. `skills-cli.test.ts` checks the exported value against core's `package.json`: the devDependency must be an exact `x.y.z` (no tag or range) and `SKILLS_CLI_VERSION` / `SKILLS_CLI_PACKAGE` must equal it. I checked that hardcoding `"skills@latest"` back into the constant makes it fail. The call-site tests keep using the constant, as you suggested.

Added two cases: a `tool_call.id` given as a number, which checks the message names `tool_call.id`, and a payload missing four required fields, which checks exactly three are listed. Each one fails if I break the matching part of the formatting (joining the path, or the `slice(0, 3)` limit).
